post.description:
Use context and a target to find the most similar points to the target, constrained by the context.
When using only the context (without a target), a special search - called context search - is performed where pairs of points are used to generate a loss that guides the search towards the zone where most positive examples overlap. This means that the score minimizes the scenario of finding a point closer to a negative than to a positive part of a pair.
Since the score of a context relates to loss, the maximum score a point can get is 0.0, and it becomes normal that many points can have a score of 0.0.
When using target (with or without context), the score behaves a little different: The integer part of the score represents the rank with respect to the context, while the decimal part of the score relates to the distance to the target. The context part of the score for each pair is calculated +1 if the point is closer to a positive than to a negative part of a pair, and -1 otherwise.

put.description:
Creates a collection with the given tenant-facing configuration. At least one dense or sparse vector is required.

The operation is idempotent on the name: if a collection with this name already exists it is left untouched and the response carries `created: false`.

single_dense.description: The simplest collection: one unnamed dense vector, default (`high`) precision, no payload indexes.

hybrid.description: Named dense and sparse vectors for hybrid search, a cheaper `medium` precision tier for the dense embeddings, IDF weighting for the BM25 sparse vector, and a few payload indexes for filtering.

multivector.description: A ColBERT / ColPali style collection: each point stores several sub-vectors that are compared with max-sim. Aggressive `low` precision keeps the many sub-vectors cheap.

time.description: Time spent to process this request, in seconds.

delete.description: Deletes the collection and all of its data. Irreversible.

result.description: `true` once the collection and its data are deleted.

Bm25Config.description: Configuration of the local bm25 models.

k.description: Controls term frequency saturation. Higher values mean term frequency has more impact. Default is 1.2

b.description: Controls document length normalization. Ranges from 0 (no normalization) to 1 (full normalization). Higher values mean longer documents have less impact. Default is 0.75.

avg_len.description: Expected average document length in the collection. Default is 256.

language.description: Defines which language to use for text preprocessing. This parameter is used to construct default stopwords filter and stemmer. To disable language-specific processing, set `stemmer` to `{"type": "none"}` and configure an empty stopword set. The legacy `"language": "none"` hack is deprecated and may be rejected in a future release. If not specified, English is assumed.

lowercase.description: Lowercase the text before tokenization. Default is `true`.

ascii_folding.description: If true, normalize tokens by folding accented characters to ASCII (e.g., "ação" -> "acao"). Default is `false`.

stopwords.description: Configuration of the stopwords filter. Supports list of pre-defined languages and custom stopwords. Default: initialized for specified `language` or English if not specified.

stemmer.description: Configuration of the stemmer. Processes tokens to their root form. Default: initialized Snowball stemmer for specified `language` or English if not specified.

min_token_len.description: Minimum token length to keep. If token is shorter than this, it will be discarded. Default is `None`, which means no minimum length.

max_token_len.description: Maximum token length to keep. If token is longer than this, it will be discarded. Default is `None`, which means no maximum length.

Mmr.description: Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR) algorithm for re-ranking the points.

diversity.description:
Tunable parameter for the MMR algorithm. Determines the balance between diversity and relevance.

A higher value favors diversity (dissimilarity to selected results), while a lower value favors relevance (similarity to the query vector).

Must be in the range [0, 1]. Default value is 0.5.

VectorNameConfig.description:
Configuration for creating a new named vector.

Contains only the immutable properties that define a vector space. Storage type, index, and quantization are determined automatically based on the segment type and can be configured separately later.

Example JSON for a dense vector: ```json { "dense": { "size": 768, "distance": "Cosine" } } ```

Example JSON for a sparse vector: ```json { "sparse": { "modifier": "Idf" } } ```

hnsw_ef.description: Params relevant to HNSW index Size of the beam in a beam-search. Larger the value - more accurate the result, more time required for search.

exact.description: Search without approximation. If set to true, search may run long but with exact results.

indexed_only.description: If enabled, the engine will only perform search among indexed or small segments. Using this option prevents slow searches in case of delayed index, but does not guarantee that all uploaded vectors will be included in search results

start_from.description: Which payload value to start scrolling from. Default is the lowest value for `asc` and the highest for `desc`

DiscoverRequest.description: Use context and a target to find the most similar points, constrained by the context.

shard_key.description: Specify in which shards to look for the points, if not specified - look in all shards

target.description:
Look for vectors closest to this.

When using the target (with or without context), the integer part of the score represents the rank with respect to the context, while the decimal part of the score relates to the distance to the target.

context.description:
Pairs of { positive, negative } examples to constrain the search.

When using only the context (without a target), a special search - called context search - is performed where pairs of points are used to generate a loss that guides the search towards the zone where most positive examples overlap. This means that the score minimizes the scenario of finding a point closer to a negative than to a positive part of a pair.

Since the score of a context relates to loss, the maximum score a point can get is 0.0, and it becomes normal that many points can have a score of 0.0.

For discovery search (when including a target), the context part of the score for each pair is calculated +1 if the point is closer to a positive than to a negative part of a pair, and -1 otherwise.

filter.description: Look only for points which satisfies this conditions

limit.description: Max number of result to return

offset.description: Offset of the first result to return. May be used to paginate results. Note: large offset values may cause performance issues.

WithVector.description: Options for specifying which vector to include

anyOf.description: If `true` - return all vector, If `false` - do not return vector

RecommendStrategy.description:
How to use positive and negative examples to find the results, default is `average_vector`:

* `average_vector` - Average positive and negative vectors and create a single query with the formula `query = avg_pos + avg_pos - avg_neg`. Then performs normal search.

* `best_score` - Uses custom search objective. Each candidate is compared against all examples, its score is then chosen from the `max(max_pos_score, max_neg_score)`. If the `max_neg_score` is chosen then it is squared and negated, otherwise it is just the `max_pos_score`.

* `sum_scores` - Uses custom search objective. Compares against all inputs, sums all the scores. Scores against positive vectors are added, against negatives are subtracted.

scale.description: The scale factor of the decay, in terms of `x`. Defaults to 1.0. Must be a non-zero positive number.

midpoint.description: The midpoint of the decay. Should be between 0 and 1.Defaults to 0.5. Output will be this value when `|x - target| == scale`.

Recommendation request. Provides positive and negative examples of the vectors, which can be ids of points that are already stored in the collection, raw vectors, or even ids and vectors combined.

Service should look for the points which are closer to positive examples and at the same time further to negative examples. The concrete way of how to compare negative and positive distances is up to the `strategy` chosen.

Read consistency parameter

Defines how many replicas should be queried to get the result

* `N` - send N random request and return points, which present on all of them

* `quorum` - send requests to all nodes and return points which present on majority of them

ServerlessDistance.description: Distance metric used to compare dense vectors. Same values as the Qdrant server API.

ServerlessPrecisionTier.description:
How much of the original vector precision may be traded for cost.

- `low`: aggressive compression, lowest cost, approximate results.
- `medium`: moderate compression with a small accuracy trade-off.
- `high`: light compression, near-exact results (default).
- `full`: no lossy compression, exact vectors fully in memory. Highest cost.

The serverless manager turns the tier into a concrete quantization and datatype choice; scalar, product or binary quantization and their parameters are never chosen directly.

ServerlessVectorsConfig.description:
Dense vectors of the collection, in one of two shapes, as in the Qdrant server API.

A single unnamed vector:

```json
{ "size": 1536, "distance": "Cosine" }
```

or several named vectors:

```json
{ "text": { "size": 1536, "distance": "Cosine" }, "image": { "size": 512, "distance": "Dot" } }
```

A collection has either the single unnamed vector or named ones, never both.

ServerlessModifier.description:
Weight modification applied to sparse vectors at query time.

- `none`: no modification (default).
- `idf`: inverse document frequency, based on statistics of the collection. Enable for BM25-style models.

ServerlessPayloadIndexType.description:
Kind of filter a payload field supports. Use the bare name when the index needs no options, e.g. `"user_id": "keyword"`.

- `keyword`: exact match on strings, e.g. `color: "red"`.
- `integer`: exact match and range filters on integers, e.g. `age: 25`.
- `float`: range filters on floating point (and integer) numbers, e.g. `price: 99.5`.
- `uuid`: exact match on UUID strings; like `keyword` but stored compactly.
- `datetime`: range filters on RFC 3339 datetimes, e.g. `created_at: "2023-02-08T10:49:00Z"`.
- `text`: full-text filtering on strings.
- `geo`: radius, bounding box and polygon filters on `{ lon, lat }` values.
- `bool`: exact match on booleans, e.g. `is_active: true`.

ServerlessIntegerIndexParams.description: Exact match and/or range filters on integers, e.g. `age: 25`. Both are on by default; turning one off shrinks the index.

ServerlessFloatIndexParams.description: Range filters on floating point (and integer) numbers, e.g. `price: 99.5`.

ServerlessUuidIndexParams.description: Exact match on UUID strings; like `keyword` but stored compactly.

ServerlessDatetimeIndexParams.description: Range filters on RFC 3339 datetimes, e.g. `created_at: "2023-02-08T10:49:00Z"`.

ServerlessGeoIndexParams.description: Geo radius, bounding box and polygon filters on `{ lon, lat }` values.

ServerlessBoolIndexParams.description: Exact match on booleans, e.g. `is_active: true`.

ServerlessTokenizer.description:
Full-text tokenizer. Same values as the Qdrant server API.

- `prefix`: index every prefix of each token.
- `whitespace`: split on whitespace (default).
- `word`: split on word boundaries.
- `multilingual`: language-aware tokenization.
- `code`: split source code into identifiers and their camelCase / snake_case subwords.

ServerlessLanguage.description: Language name as accepted by the Qdrant server API, lowercase, e.g. `english`, `german`, `spanish`.

ServerlessStopwords.description: Tokens to ignore at index and query time. Either a single language name, e.g. `"english"`, or a set combining several languages and custom tokens.

ServerlessSnowballParams.description: Snowball stemmer for the given language.

ServerlessDisabledStemmerParams.description: Explicitly disable stemming (overrides any language default).

ServerlessNestedPayloadIndex.description: Index every object of this array as a separate entry, e.g. `offers` for the field `offers[].price`. The indexed field must be inside the array's elements. `is_empty` on the field matches a point when one of its elements lacks the field, and never a point without elements. Unset: disabled.

ServerlessTextScoringType.description: How a text index ranks documents.

ServerlessTextScoringParams.description: Parameters of ranking over a text index. The index records the length of each document, which BM25 normalizes by. `k` and `b` are set per query.

ServerlessTextScoring.description: BM25 scoring for a text index: `true` for the default parameters, `false` to disable it, or the parameters themselves. Changing it rebuilds the index. Default: disabled.

ServerlessStemmingAlgorithm.description: Stemming algorithm for a full-text index. Unset: no stemming.

lowercase.description: Lowercase text before indexing. Default: true.

phrase_matching.description: Support phrase queries; builds extra index structure. Default: true.

ascii_folding.description: Fold accented characters to ASCII (e.g. `ação` -> `acao`). Default: false.

nested.description: Index every object of this array as a separate entry, e.g. `offers` for the field `offers[].title`. The field must be inside the array's elements. Every query on the field, not only nested filters, treats each element as its own document: a condition matches a point when a single element matches it, and BM25 scores elements separately. `is_empty` on the field matches a point when one of its elements lacks the field, and never a point without elements. Default: disabled.

ServerlessPayloadIndexConfig.description:
One payload index, as in the Qdrant server API: either the bare index type, e.g. `"keyword"`, or an object with options, e.g. `{ "type": "text", "tokenizer": "word" }`.

Only the kind of filter the field supports is chosen here; storage placement of the index is the manager's decision.

- `green`: all segments are optimized.
- `yellow`: optimization is pending or running; the collection stays searchable.

- `pending`: some acknowledged writes are still queued and not yet visible to search.

The tenant-facing configuration of a collection. Unlike the Qdrant server API it is deliberately small: the serverless manager turns it into concrete Qdrant settings (HNSW, quantization, storage placement, ...), which are never exposed.

At least one dense or sparse vector is required.
